_comment: The scale column. Buildings fall away beside the diver; the UI stacks them to express depth. Bangkok entries are deliberate - the room is at Chulalongkorn, and a building the audience can see from the venue lands harder than one they cannot.
_usage: Pick the tallest building whose height is <= current depth, and show floor(depth / height) stacked. Below ~1,000 m switch to the tallest entry only, or the column becomes absurd - which is the point, so say it in words instead: 'thirteen Mahanakhons'.

buildings.name: Big Ben
buildings.note: The tower, properly the Elizabeth Tower.

buildings.name: Eiffel Tower
buildings.note: To the tip, including the antennas added in 2022.

buildings.name: King Power Mahanakhon
buildings.note: 314.2 m. The pixelated one. Visible from most of central Bangkok.

buildings.name: Magnolias Waterfront
buildings.note: 317.95 m, at ICONSIAM. Currently the tallest building in Thailand.

buildings.name: Empire State Building
buildings.note: To the tip of the antenna; 381 m to the roof.

buildings.name: Merdeka 118
buildings.note: 678.9 m. The second tallest building in the world.

buildings.name: Burj Khalifa
buildings.note: The tallest building in the world. It takes four and a half of them, stacked, to reach the Titanic.

milestones.line: The continental shelf breaks here, and you are not yet one Eiffel Tower down.
The deepest scuba dive ever made. Exactly one Eiffel Tower.
Two and a half Eiffel Towers down, and there is no light left worth the name.
The deepest dive by any mammal. Nine Eiffel Towers.
The Titanic. Eleven and a half Eiffel Towers, stacked.
The deepest octopus ever filmed. Twenty-one Eiffel Towers.
The deepest fish ever filmed. Below this, no fish at all.
The bottom. Thirty-three Eiffel Towers, straight down.
